solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: post-colon clause ('nearly every roadside, fence line and riverbank') nearly defines 'ubiquitous'; A/B/C are easy eliminations (endangered contradicts spread, dormant contradicts growing, ornamental contrasts with gardens rather than spread)
S033-01.notes: Spread from a few gardens to nearly everywhere = ubiquitous. Only 'ubiquitous' vocabulary may slow weaker readers.

flags: minor: 'finished' is the direct antonym and 'extravagant' contradicts leaving land unbuilt; distractors weak
S033-02.notes: Leaving room to extend and add buildings later = open-ended.

flags: minor: the key introduces 'hidden ocean', which the passage never mentions; students must infer a subsurface water source from the water-vapor plumes. Consider adding a sentence that Enceladus has an ocean beneath its ice to make the inference fully text-based
minor: science is accurate (Hsu et al. 2015, Cassini nanosilica grains implying hydrothermal activity at rock-water interface)
S033-03.notes: Silica of that size forms when rock-dissolving hot water cools quickly, so water on Enceladus is hot where it contacts rock. A contradicts the Earth analogy; C contradicts 'water vapor'; D overgeneralizes to the surface.

S033-04.notes: If snails still withdraw instantly to a new stimulus, the withdrawal response is not exhausted, ruling out fatigue and supporting stimulus-specific learning (habituation). B supports fatigue; A is compatible with either (fatigue would also be faster with closer taps); D is the baseline already stated.

flags: minor: key is the only choice that computes differences and is noticeably longer/more specific; B, C, D each address only part of the claim, which savvy test-takers may spot quickly
S033-05.notes: Extra insects: white 120-10=110, amber 45-10=35. 35 vs 110 shows large reduction (~68%) but not elimination (35>0). Arithmetic verified. B supports 'reduce' but not 'not eliminate'.

flags: minor: key is the only hedged choice ('may have mattered alongside'), a mild answer cue
minor: Text 2 never explicitly mentions climate; 'less able to withstand hard years' implies a compatible, additive view, which is reasonable but inferential
S033-06.notes: Text 2 adds an economic factor that weakened resilience to hard years, not a rejection of cooling. A overstates; B misreads (demand fell, not hunting ability); C contradicts Text 2.

flags: minor: 'the rock' in B has no antecedent within the sentence (should be 'a space rock')
minor: facts check out (June 30, 1908; ~80 million trees over ~2,150 km2; Kulik expedition 1927; no crater; airburst consensus)
S033-07.notes: Only B gives the reason (damage but no crater). D states the conclusion without explanation; A and C are irrelevant to 'why'.

S033-08.notes: Second sentence gives specific design features illustrating the energy-saving claim. Nevertheless/Instead imply contrast; Previously is wrong in time (these are features of the new building).

flags: minor: fact check fine (coelacanth thought extinct since end of Cretaceous; found off South Africa 1938)
S033-09.notes: Appositive closed by a dash must be opened by a dash. Comma (A) is the common trap because commas usually mark appositives; semicolon and no punctuation are clearly wrong.

flags: minor: collective-noun agreement; British usage would accept 'their', but SAT conventions treat 'the city council' as singular, so A is uniquely correct
S033-10.notes: Singular possessive referring to 'the city council' = its. 'their' is the main trap (council members); it's/they're are contractions and ungrammatical here.
